G0 · render check · 60 Cycles clips · motion guard

What the judge was actually being shown

Two earlier G0 runs concluded the judge had no stable material preference. They were measured on clips where the entire drop, bounce and settle happened between the judge’s first and second frame. This page shows the rendering and the video experiment so the setup can be checked directly, not just the statistics.

Defect 1 — the clips were nearly static

The judge received 10 frames. This is how many of the 9 consecutive differences contained any motion, on the clips each stage actually scored.

Drop height was lowered 0.30 → 0.15 m to stop objects rolling off the table — undoing a change made in J2 for exactly this reason — and the frame budget was never rechecked. Every result after that change was measured on a still life.

Defect 2 — EEVEE renders metal wrong

EEVEE Next defaults to use_raytracing = False, so there are no reflections. Rows 1–2 are the brass pot in EEVEE then Cycles; rows 3–4 the duck. The Cycles pot is polished copper with a tabletop reflection; the EEVEE pot is a dark matte lump. That breaks rule 2 (fixed target-material appearance) on the object whose preference flipped hardest. The engine swap had been validated by correlating scores, never by looking at it.

The fix, and what the judge sees now

  • Trim to the event window, computed from the simulated height. This cuts the roll-away tail — the thing the drop height was lowered to avoid — so the drop goes back to 0.30 m and the motion returns. One change, both problems.
  • Fixed 12 frames spanning the clip, not a fixed 4 fps. A trimmed event is ~0.5–1 s; at 4 fps that is 2–4 frames, trading one starvation for another. Judge change ⇒ rule 3 ⇒ this recalibration.
  • Cycles, not EEVEE.
  • A motion guard that refuses to score any clip whose sampled frames are more than 40% static. It would have blocked J3 before it ran.

Every clip, and its guard result

All 60. Guard passed 56/60; motion fraction median 1.00 against 0.11–0.22 before. Rejected clips are outlined and were not scored.

Result

Pre-registered in 9730fbd before this run saw data; the statistic and pass rule are byte-identical to the earlier registration in ce7bc5d. Primary is the partial Spearman ρ(margin, Δe | Δlog M, Δμ), bootstrap 95% CI. PASS needs duck > 0 and pot < 0, both CIs excluding zero, gap > 0.5, in both friction halves.

What to be suspicious of

  • Three changes at once. Trim, decode and engine all moved together. A pass licenses this configuration; it does not say which fix mattered.
  • High-e clips still travel. ρ(e, travel) is +0.67 for the duck and +0.73 for the pot, and 10 of 56 clips move more than 0.5 m — some leave the frame before the clip ends. The primary statistic partials out pixel-motion magnitude, but “object exits view” is a categorical difference that magnitude only partly captures.
  • Position bias remains large. In the previous run the A-slot preference was ~15× the content margin, with 100% of pairs favouring slot A. Order-averaging removes it in expectation but the margin stays a small difference of two large numbers.
  • Only two objects. The ceramic vase showed no restitution preference at all under pairwise scoring earlier, so a duck/pot contrast holding is not evidence the signal generalises.
